title: Exclusive: Vienna’s fonio.ai hits $10m ARR less than a year after switching on subscriptions
excerpt: fonio.ai, the Vienna voice-AI startup, says it has passed $10m in annual recurring revenue in under a year, growing more than 30% a month since it went subscription-only.
content_html:
Vienna startup most of the tech world has not heard of just posted numbers that would turn heads anywhere. fonio.ai, a European platform for AI-powered customer calls, says it has surpassed $10m in annual recurring revenue in under twelve months.

Since February, when the company switched from a prepaid model to subscriptions, it says it has grown revenue by more than 30% a month, a compounding run that has carried it from a standing start into eight-figure territory.

What fonio.ai sells is automated conversation; its AI agents answer the phone, handle WhatsApp and will soon manage email and chat too, holding natural-sounding conversations for businesses that field high volumes of customer contact around the clock.

The scale is already substantial as the company says it serves more than 7,000 customers and runs several million calls through its platform every month, the kind of volume that turns a clever demo into a genuine operational tool.

In June, fonio.ai closed a $17M seed round led by Harry Stebbings’ 20VC at a $140m valuation, reportedly one of the largest seed rounds Austria has ever seen, only months after an earlier raise.

“We are building a global market leader, and we are building it out of Vienna,” says co-founder and chief executive Daniel Keinrath, who started the company in late 2024 with Matthias Gruber.

The pitch rests on owning more of the stack than rivals do. fonio.ai produces its own voices, which it says sound hyper-realistic and rank among the best available in many languages, rather than leaning entirely on the human-realistic voice tools that have become widely available to everyone.

It is also leaning into personalisation. Its agents are designed to learn from the calls they handle, and the platform can recognise returning callers to greet them by name or recall their details, a feature it says is GDPR-compliant and has to be switched on deliberately.

Customer-service lines are expensive to staff and notoriously hard to keep running around the clock, so an agent that answers instantly, in a caller’s own language and at any hour, targets one of the clearest cost centres a company has.

The company is not shy about where it thinks this goes. fonio.ai is targeting annual recurring revenue of €20m to €30m by the end of the year, which would more than double the milestone it is now celebrating.

Moreover, the company made its first hire only in June 2025 and already counts around 80 staff, with 17 joining last month alone, 52 roles open, and a target of 130 to 150 people by year-end across ten markets.

It has grown by acquisition as well as recruitment, having bought its Linz-based rival fluently last September, a sign that it intends to consolidate its home region rather than merely defend it.

The competition, though, is exactly the catch. Well-funded American rivals such as HappyRobot, fresh off a $150m round, are chasing the same enterprise buyers, and the model labs keep folding ever-better voices into their own products.

There are the usual caveats to a company-announced milestone, too. ARR is self-reported and unaudited, blistering monthly growth is far easier from a small base than a large one, and the hard questions of gross margin, churn and profitability sit outside a celebratory headline.

fonio.ai co-founder and chief executive Daniel Keinrath talked with us and gave some insights on the matter.

$10m ARR in twelve months is exceptional. How much of that is net-new customers versus expansion within existing accounts, and what is your net revenue retention?

Daniel Keinrath: We don’t want to share our exact revenue composition, but we can share that our current NRR is a little under 100%. The goal is to reach 110% until EOY.

Churn tends to be the quiet killer for AI companies that are growing fast. What are your logo and revenue churn rates, and how did the prepaid-to-subscription switch change them?

Daniel Keinrath: We can’t share our exact churn, but I can share that it helps a lot that we don’t have a free trial. We work with a hard paywall. Therefore the buy-in of our customers is quite high and we have a very solid churn-rate for an AI startup.

Your agents “learn from the conversations they hold.” What exactly are they learning, how do you stop them from learning the wrong things, and how can a customer audit that?

Daniel Keinrath: Our customers automatically get a list of proposals that should be added to the knowledge base. They can review it and accept / decline / improve the suggestions. In 95% of the cases our customers just accept the improvements of the knowledge base.

You talk about building a global market leader out of Vienna. Can a European voice-AI company really win globally, or will the US market eventually pull your centre of gravity across the Atlantic?

Daniel Keinrath: I think we currently have one of the best shots to win our market segment globally. We are based in Europe, but work with a US mindset and US intensity. Also, our 17m seed round would have also been in the top 1-2% of US seed rounds.

For fonio.ai, the challenge now is the one Daniel Keinrath named himself: turning a spectacular twelve months into a durable, global business.

fonio.ai 卖的是自动对话；其人工智能代理可以接听电话、处理 WhatsApp，并且很快还将管理电子邮件和聊天，为全天候与大量客户联系的企业进行听起来自然的对话。

该公司表示，其规模已经相当大，为 7,000 多名客户提供服务，每月通过其平台运行数百万个呼叫，这种规模可以将巧妙的演示转变为真正的操作工具。

6 月，fonio.ai 完成了由 Harry Stebbings 的 20VC 领投的 1700 万美元种子轮融资，估值为 1.4 亿美元，据报道，这是奥地利有史以来最大的种子轮融资之一，距离之前的融资仅几个月。

联合创始人兼首席执行官 Daniel Keinrath 表示：“我们正在打造一个全球市场领导者，而且我们正在维也纳之外打造它。”他于 2024 年底与 Matthias Gruber 共同创立了这家公司。

优势在于拥有比竞争对手更多的筹码。 fonio.ai 产生自己的声音，据称这些声音听起来超现实，并且在许多语言中名列前茅，而不是完全依赖于每个人都可以广泛使用的逼真语音工具。

它还倾向于个性化。 其代理旨在从他们处理的呼叫中学习，并且该平台可以识别回拨电话，以名字问候他们或回忆他们的详细信息，据称该功能符合 GDPR 标准，必须有意开启。

客户服务热线对员工来说成本高昂，而且众所周知很难保持全天候运行，因此，一个能够在任何时间、用呼叫者的母语立即应答的客服人员，瞄准了公司最清晰的成本中心之一。

该公司并不羞于透露自己的想法。 fonio.ai 的目标是到今年年底，年度经常性收入达到 2000 万欧元至 3000 万欧元，这将是其目前庆祝的里程碑的两倍多。

此外，该公司于 2025 年 6 月才首次招聘员工，目前已有约 80 名员工，仅上个月就有 17 名员工加入，还有 52 个职位空缺，目标是到年底在 10 个市场招聘 130 至 150 名员工。

它通过收购和招聘实现了增长，去年九月顺利收购了总部位于林茨的竞争对手，这表明它打算巩固其本土地区，而不仅仅是保卫它。

然而，竞争正是问题所在。 资金雄厚的美国竞争对手，例如刚完成 1.5 亿美元融资的 HappyRobot，正在追逐同样的企业买家，而模型实验室也不断将更好的声音融入到自己的产品中。

对于公司宣布的里程碑，也有一些常见的警告。 ARR 是自我报告且未经审计的，小基数比大基数更容易实现惊人的月度增长，而毛利率、客户流失率和盈利能力等难题则不属于值得庆祝的头条新闻。

fonio.ai 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Daniel Keinrath 与我们进行了交谈，并就此事给出了一些见解。

12 个月内实现 1000 万美元的 ARR 是非常罕见的。 其中有多少是净新客户与现有客户的扩张相比，您的净收入保留是多少？

Daniel Keinrath：我们不想透露我们的确切收入构成，但我们可以告诉大家，我们目前的 NRR 略低于 100%。 目标是到年底前达到 110%。

对于快速发展的人工智能公司来说，流失往往是悄无声息的杀手。 您的徽标和收入流失率是多少？从预付费到订阅的转变如何改变了它们？

Daniel Keinrath：我们无法透露确切的流失情况，但我可以分享的是，我们没有免费试用，这对我们有很大帮助。 我们采用硬付费墙。 因此，我们客户的认可度相当高，对于一家人工智能初创公司来说，我们的客户流失率非常高。

您的代理“从他们进行的对话中学习”。 他们究竟在学习什么，如何阻止他们学习错误的东西，以及客户如何审核这些内容？

Daniel Keinrath：我们的客户会自动获得应添加到知识库中的提案列表。 他们可以审查并接受/拒绝/改进建议。 在 95% 的情况下，我们的客户只是接受知识库的改进。

您谈到在维也纳建立全球市场领导者。 欧洲语音人工智能公司真的能在全球赢得胜利吗？还是美国市场最终会把你的重心拉到大西洋彼岸？

Daniel Keinrath：我认为我们目前拥有赢得全球细分市场的最佳机会之一。 我们的总部设在欧洲，但以美国的心态和强度开展工作。 此外，我们的 1700 万种子轮也将进入美国种子轮的前 1-2%。

对于 fonio.ai 来说，现在的挑战是 Daniel Keinrath 自己所说的挑战：将辉煌的 12 个月转变为持久的全球业务。
